status: interface contract for phase 6; this file is not a pipeline implementation

selected_backend.threads_note: thread sweep in evidence/voice/P5/20260917/threads/ measured 2/3/4/6 threads on the A76 cluster at 0.294/0.255/0.356/0.706 RTF P95 and 1.339 on 4 A55 little cores; 3 threads on the big cluster is the measured optimum and the full-stack run at 3 threads met both objectives
selected_backend.license: model code Apache-2.0; training dataset Baker (DataBaker) NON-COMMERCIAL - valid only under the 2026-09-17 decision that this project is non-commercial

shape.load: load the engine; timing is reported separately and must never be charged to first-segment latency
shape.synthesize: synthesize one text segment, return TtsResult
shape.first_audible_s: seconds from generation start to the first sample above -45 dBFS sustained 20 ms; NOT the same as the first callback
shape.cache: TtsBackend caches by exact text, which is how pre-generated status PCM is served

guarantees: no pipeline, no queues, no threads, no audio device access in this layer
raises TtsError on empty text, NaN/Inf samples, empty PCM or silent audio
engine construction lives in one place so the benchmark and the runtime cannot drift

rules.strict_first_segment: the first segment is released at the first sentence-final punctuation, or at first_max_characters; it is never soft-cut early into a half phrase
rules.later_segments: cut at sentence punctuation, else at clause punctuation once the target length is reached, else at the target length; the hard cap is never exceeded
rules.lookahead: the soft cut keeps one character of lookahead so a clause mark arriving on the boundary is not orphaned into the next segment

segmentation_parameters.note: first_max_characters is the latency/prosody knob. The measured curve shows the selected Matcha backend remains within the 0.8 s objective through 24 characters, so the runtime now uses 24 to avoid cutting ordinary Chinese sentences too early.

measured_first_segment_curve.backend: matcha-icefall-zh-baker, 4 threads, A76, idle bench, 5 runs per length
interpretation: up to about 24 characters (about 4.8 s of audio) the first callback arrives early and the delivered chunk grows with the segment
beyond that the first callback effectively carries the whole segment and latency grows linearly with audio duration
so the safe first-segment budget is <= 16 characters, and 24 characters is the measured upper bound
late segments may be long: at 120 characters RTF is still about 0.10, so throughput is not the constraint

acoustic_reference.method: gated 250 ms pilot bursts; the offset is the delay between handing PCM to ALSA and the microphone picking the sound up
acoustic_reference.consequence: acoustic_first_sound ~= software first_valid_pcm; do not add a large fixed acoustic allowance
acoustic_reference.environments_note: at the default low speaker level the room floor is about -40 dBFS and per-utterance acoustic detection is unreliable; per-utterance acoustic checks must be run at a raised, explicitly recorded level

pre_generated_pcm.principle: fixed status phrases may be pre-generated, but playback must be triggered by the real state machine and must never be counted as a dynamic-answer first-sound measurement
pre_generated_pcm.implementation: synthesize once at startup through TtsBackend.synthesize(); the result is cached by exact text, so a hit costs a dictionary lookup and no synthesis
pre_generated_pcm.not_a_substitute_for: dynamic Qwen answers, which must go through real synthesis

must_handle: whole-machine available memory measured at 1167 MiB for a single configured stack and as low as 745 MiB when other workload shares the board; the 1024 MiB guard used by P3 has little margin
the 2-character case shows RTF up to 0.726 at 3 threads and 0.866 at 4 threads; either cover very short playbacks with pre-generated PCM or accept and document it
pre-generated PCM must be state-triggered, never scheduled unconditionally
must_not_do: grow the playback buffer to hide a synthesis gap
treat the sherpa-onnx callback as a streaming guarantee
charge cold model load to first-segment latency

conclusions: 3 threads on the A76 cluster is the measured optimum; 6 threads is worse than 4
pinning to the A76 cluster is mandatory: the little cluster cannot keep up (RTF P95 1.339 > 1)
load time is insensitive to thread count (3.48-3.74 s)
